Project-local config, hooks, and exec policies are disabled in the following folders until the project is trusted, but skills still load.
    1. /work/.codex
       To load project-local config, hooks, and exec policies, add /work as a trusted project in /home/worker/.codex/config.toml.

skills.name: Zotero
skills.description: Use Zotero Desktop from Codex to search a local library, verify reference metadata and recommendation evidence, read indexed full text when requested, export BibTeX, insert citation keys, and import verified records. Never invent references or fill bibliographic gaps from memory.

interface.shortDescription: Verify references and add Zotero citations
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $Zotero to verify references, search my library, and add grounded citations to my draft.

skills.name: aar
skills.description: Conduct an After Action Review of completed or interrupted work, comparing expectations with outcomes and capturing successful practices, lessons, and follow-up actions. Use for broad task or team retrospectives; use RCA for deeper investigation of a specific failure.

interface.shortDescription: Review outcomes and turn lessons into owned actions
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $aar to review this completed work and identify practices to sustain and change.

skills.name: analysis-router
skills.description: Select and coordinate AAR, RCA, RMEA, FTA, MCDA, risk planning, ADR, and verification workflows when a request crosses their boundaries or needs multiple analyses. Resolve consequential ambiguity by comparing candidate workflows independently through auto-subagents; skip routing overhead for an obvious local task.

interface.shortDescription: Select analysis methods and compare boundary cases
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $analysis-router to select the appropriate analysis and compare competing methods if needed.

skills.name: archify
skills.description: Create validated architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, lifecycle/state, ERD, class, tree, timeline, and waterfall diagrams as explorable standalone HTML with dark/light themes, motion and image/SVG/WebM export. Accept requirements or Mermaid; inspect repository evidence for code-backed diagrams. Use when visualizing systems, API calls, pipelines, schemas, histories, timings, or everyday steps, parts, relationships and states. Also turn an answer into a one-page explainer, with the conclusion first, structured panels, native diagrams and charts, when the user asks for a page, an explainer or an answer to share (做成一页, 用页面讲), or proactively when the user's rules opt in with an [archify explainer: ...] line. Not for dashboards.

interface.shortDescription: Create validated diagrams and one-page explainers
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $archify to create a validated diagram or one-page explainer for this topic.

skills.name: architecture-decision-record
skills.description: Create, amend, supersede, and audit Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) documenting architectural choices, alternative options, evidence, trade-offs, risk ownership, consequences, and reversal triggers. Use when a technical decision is proposed, accepted, revisited, or reversed; pair with project-plan for branching project plans.

interface.shortDescription: Record architectural choices, trade-offs, and review triggers
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $architecture-decision-record to record this material decision, its alternatives, evidence, risks, and conditions for revisiting it.

skills.name: auto-skill-manager
skills.description: Use when the user asks which skills fit a project or task, requests skill/plugin-package inventory or observation review, or asks for scoped Skill Manager CLI maintenance. Use skill-creator to author skill content and plugin-management for external app integrations.

skills.name: auto-subagents
skills.description: Assess and coordinate useful parallel work and subagent delegation across tasks, including investigation, implementation, and verification, when independence and expected benefit justify the overhead.

interface.shortDescription: Coordinate useful delegation with bounded context
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $auto-subagents to delegate independent work when it improves this task.

skills.name: create-gui
skills.description: Design and build new stateful desktop operator GUI projects through a persistent, multi-session requirements interview, documented approval gate, implementation, and interaction/error-path verification. Applies to hardware-backed, simulation, replay, and data-driven operator applications; do not route ordinary small edits to an established GUI here.

interface.shortDescription: 설계 인터뷰부터 검증까지 진행하는 오퍼레이터 GUI 제작
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $create-gui to interview me and create a new operator GUI project.

skills.name: design-boundaries
skills.description: Design responsibility, dependency, state, and lifecycle boundaries for new systems, substantial features, or scoped architectural redesigns. Use when multiple capabilities or resource owners must collaborate; do not trigger for routine local fixes or split modules solely by line count.

interface.shortDescription: Design module ownership and dependency boundaries
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $design-boundaries to define responsibilities, interfaces, ownership, and lifecycle boundaries for this feature.

skills.name: explain-xlsx
skills.description: Create formula-traceable XLSX workbooks alongside code-derived numerical results. Use across simulation, research, engineering, analytics, operations, and other quantitative projects when producing a reportable result artifact, or when asked to explain calculations in a workbook. Not for routine data export or unrelated spreadsheet editing.

interface.shortDescription: Trace code calculations into reviewable XLSX
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $explain-xlsx to turn these code-derived results into a traceable XLSX.

skills.name: faust
skills.description: Estimate the probability of a defined event using information available at a cutoff. Use for prospective forecasts, historical case exercises from supplied evidence, and scoring resolved predictions. Also supports stock research and RIS project handoffs.

interface.shortDescription: Forecast event probabilities from dated evidence
interface.defaultPrompt: $faust 이 자료의 기준 시점까지 알려진 정보로, 주어진 기한 안에 사건이 일어날 확률과 그 근거를 설명해 줘.

skills.name: fta
skills.description: Perform Fault Tree Analysis of a defined undesirable event using AND/OR logic, event definitions, minimal cut sets, and mitigations. Use for prospective failure-path analysis or incident hypotheses; an FTA alone does not establish the actual cause of an incident.

interface.shortDescription: Model failure combinations and minimal cut sets
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $fta to model this top failure event with explicit assumptions and minimal cut sets.

skills.name: maintain-boundaries
skills.description: Keep responsibility, dependency, state, and lifecycle boundaries intact while extending or refactoring existing code. Use for cross-module changes, shared resource or contract changes, and edits to highly coupled controllers; do not require architecture reviews for trivial local edits.

interface.shortDescription: Preserve module boundaries while changing code
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $maintain-boundaries to keep responsibility, state ownership, and dependencies coherent during this change.

skills.name: mcda
skills.description: Compare alternatives using Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis with explicit criteria, scales, weights, evidence, and sensitivity analysis. Use for consequential trade-offs across multiple criteria; record architectural decisions in an available ADR workflow when appropriate.

interface.shortDescription: Compare options with weighted values and sensitivity
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $mcda to compare these alternatives with explicit preferences, evidence, and sensitivity.

skills.name: modify-gui
skills.description: Modify an existing stateful desktop operator GUI and the backend behavior directly required by that GUI through persistent change interviews, impact analysis, explicit approval, implementation, and end-to-end regression verification. Applies to hardware-backed, simulation, replay, and data-driven operator applications; do not route tiny isolated presentation fixes or backend work unrelated to a user-visible GUI contract here.

interface.shortDescription: 기존 오퍼레이터 GUI와 연결 백엔드를 안전하게 수정
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $modify-gui to interview me and safely modify this operator GUI.

skills.name: project-plan
skills.description: Design or revise consequential project plans with branching choices, quality gates, fallback routes, and evidence-based switch criteria. Coordinate specialist risk or option analysis only when needed; standalone risk registers belong to RMEA, weighted alternative evaluation to MCDA, and material architectural decision history to ADR.

interface.shortDescription: Map outcome elements, forecasts, choices and verification paths
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $project-plan to connect desired outcomes to evidence-backed alternatives, forecast their consequences and generate an interactive HTML decision map with verification and fallback paths.

skills.name: rca
skills.description: Investigate actual important failures, recurring defects, and unexplained outcome gaps using causal hypotheses, supporting and contrary evidence, and corrective-action checks. Use AAR for overall retrospectives and FTA for modeled failure combinations; obvious local errors need no formal RCA.

interface.shortDescription: Investigate failures with evidence and causal checks
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $rca to investigate this failure, test causal hypotheses, and propose verifiable corrective actions.

skills.name: research-audit
skills.description: Independently audit RIS research coverage, evidence quality, causal integrity, plan feasibility, and conditional forecasts before project pre-analysis is accepted.

interface.shortDescription: Independently audit RIS research and project forecasts
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $research-audit to inspect this RIS analysis against its goal, evidence, plan, assumptions, and forecasts.

skills.name: reviewer
skills.description: 연구 논문, 기술 보고서, 발표자료를 엄격하고 근거 중심으로 심사해 거절·감점 위험, 근거 부족, 우선순위별 보완안을 제시할 때 사용합니다.

interface.shortDescription: 논문·보고서·발표자료를 근거 중심으로 엄격히 심사합니다
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $reviewer to review my research paper in Korean as a strict, evidence-based reviewer.

skills.name: ris
skills.description: Initialize or resume project-local research, align the agent with the user's background, investigate phenomena, causes and solution families, organize source-backed learning and branching plans, and record findings or handoffs in Markdown for Obsidian. Use for RIS requests and research continuity in initialized projects. Also use for explicit requests to diagnose or improve the RIS skill or its role instructions. Do not initialize unrelated projects or record every conversation automatically.

interface.shortDescription: Restore project context and organize source-backed research
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $ris to restore this project's context, continue source-backed research, and link findings to its canonical project plan.

skills.name: rmea
skills.description: Perform Risk Mode and Effect Analysis to identify potential risk modes, their causes and impacts, existing controls, response priorities, and residual risk. Use for structured prospective risk assessment; use FTA for logical combinations producing a specific failure.

interface.shortDescription: Assess risk modes, controls and residual risk
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $rmea to assess prospective risks, prioritize controls, and identify residual uncertainty.

skills.name: skill-auto-manager
skills.description: Find and compare reusable products, components, projects, tools, skills and plugins when planning a system or substantial feature, investigating existing alternatives, authoring skills, or addressing capability gaps and repeated manual work. Apply even when the user does not mention skills or plugins. Also review installed skill coverage and inventory. Skip routine work already covered; use skill-creator for authoring and plugin-management for app connections.

interface.shortDescription: Find reusable projects, tools, skills and plugins
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $skill-auto-manager to compare existing projects, tools, skills and plugins before choosing what to reuse or build.

skills.name: teach-me
skills.description: Explain a real computation, algorithm, formula, or code path so a non-specialist can reproduce a worked example by hand. Use when the user explicitly asks to learn how a calculation works step by step, not for a short definition or routine code summary.

interface.shortDescription: Learn real computations with hand-checkable examples
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $teach-me to explain this computation step by step with a reproducible example.

skills.name: update-architecture
skills.description: Refresh a project's current architecture documents and non-expert HTML reader only when explicitly requested, preserving separate change explanations and verified evidence.

skills.name: verify-check
skills.description: Split substantial code or behavior changes into small, independently verifiable steps, verify their handoffs, and validate the original user workflow. Use for multi-step or cross-layer implementation, fixes, and reviews; scale checks to risk. Use rca when failures need deeper cause analysis.

interface.shortDescription: Split changes into small, independently verified slices
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $verify-check to split this change into small slices and verify each with independent evidence.

skills.name: create-statusline
skills.description: Build and enable a custom MCP statusline for the Codex CLI. Use when someone wants a provider that displays information in the terminal footer.

skills.name: imagegen
skills.description: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas.

interface.shortDescription: Generate or edit images for websites, games, and more
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $imagegen to make or edit an image for this project.

skills.name: openai-docs
skills.description: API first-timers, Codex/Work Q&A. If the user already has an OpenAI API integration, skip this skill for API questions and use the developer docs. Read this skill before answering how Codex or ChatGPT Work behaves, where to find a feature, or how to configure or troubleshoot this app or coding agent. This includes conversation history, model and cache behavior, instruction precedence, permissions, and tool availability. Use for API onboarding only when the user is connecting to the OpenAI API for the first time. Skip action requests, such as scheduling an automation, and tasks fully answered by supplied text or data.

interface.shortDescription: Codex and ChatGPT Work Q&A, plus first-time API setup
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $openai-docs to explain a Codex or ChatGPT Work feature, help with my first OpenAI API integration, or migrate a request to my chosen model.

skills.name: review-agent
skills.description: Perform a read-only, defect-first review of a specified code change and return every actionable finding. Use when another agent delegates review of uncommitted changes, a base-branch diff, a commit, or custom review instructions.

interface.shortDescription: Find actionable bugs in code changes
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $review-agent to review the requested code changes and return actionable findings.

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.description: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources.

interface.shortDescription: Create or update a skill

skills.name: skill-installer
skills.description: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos).
skills.shortDescription: Install curated skills from openai/skills or other repos

interface.shortDescription: Install curated skills from openai/skills or other repos
